evidence: The frozen workbook Quality Checks!D39 requires each scored prompt to score criteria independently and continue after failure; Internal Quality Checks!D39 agrees, and the skill quality procedure 38 and deterministic reference line54 require the same. All three scored judge configurations use batched mode and weighted_mean. In frozen task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:11, the judge must "score EACH criterion independently, continue after failure, and preserve successful observations"; it also prohibits carrying a sibling verdict, permits simpler fresh setup, and preserves completed observations when a tool or budget prevents another observation. Lines19,35,47,53,65 reinforce independent shared-protocol facts and alternate setup. task/tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:8 explicitly says "judge each criterion independently, continue after failures"; lines10 and16 preserve independent recovery observations. task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:8 requires independent anchored scoring and continuation, while lines10,12 prohibit double deductions and preserve completed observations. Injected app_context.md contains no stop-on-failure direction. Targeted scans of all injected criterion descriptions found no instruction to stop the batch or inherit a sibling failure; functional/judge.toml:704-722 expressly separates concurrent approval/revision/rescission credit, and :731-785 separates confidential data families from anonymous status. These agree with the frozen template independent-scoring clauses and current review policy. Local Python -B source assertions confirmed all three prompts contain independence and continue-after-failure wording; this was a local source check, not execution of the private checker or a configured app judge. Raw evidence index SHA256 56cf3afb78d5256d0b90ebe7a89f9f3e8174d5aca3787eb918d6954d6388c1a7 has the assigned input hash; all 307 referenced artifact hashes matched at review. No app-grade, workload, Oracle or portal claim is made; those measurements are not required to establish this prompt-wording row.
counterexample: Reasoned broken alternative: an app approves normally but mishandles concurrent same-target approval while ordinary revision/rescission work. Functional prompt:47 and judge.toml:713,722 require fresh eligible targets and independent later verdicts, so the failed approval pair cannot zero those successes. A shared bootstrap that leaks only offers also cannot erase proven equity/referral confidentiality (prompt:45 and criterion clauses:731-785); each actual leak still fails its own row. Reasoned conforming alternative: an initially empty operational desk with generated IDs, different layouts and a read-only retained-date Retry confirmation remains assessable (instruction.md:5,11; functional prompt:13; visual prompt:8; polish judge.toml:32). If tooling cannot intercept that conforming retry, polish prompt:16 labels only missing observations as evaluator limitations and preserves completed sibling credit. No row38 false-pass or cascading false-fail instruction was found; alternatives were source reasoning, not measured app runs.
